text: A fundamental optical soliton in a fiber propagates without spreading because of a balance between two effects. Which two?
choices: Chromatic dispersion and ordinary linear loss
Anomalous group-velocity dispersion (β₂ < 0) and Kerr self-phase modulation
explanation: The nonlinear Schrödinger equation admits a soliton when anomalous GVD (β₂ < 0) exactly cancels the chirp from Kerr self-phase modulation (γ|A|²). Normal dispersion (β₂ > 0) reinforces rather than cancels the SPM chirp, and scattering or linear loss are dissipative, not the dispersive/nonlinear balance that sustains a soliton.
